title: B1 · L45 — Money & personal finance
description: Vocabulario financiero personal: save, invest, budget, debt, loan, expenses, income, afford.

questions.prompt: Situación: describes tu estrategia de ahorro personal.
questions.question: Choose: 'I try to ___ some money every month for holidays.'
questions.explanation: 'Save money' = ahorrar. Verbo clave de finanzas personales. Error típico del hispanohablante: '*safe money*' — falso amigo con 'safe' (seguro). Colocaciones: 'save money for + meta', 'save up for + meta grande'. 'Spend' es lo contrario, 'earn' es ganar, 'lose' es perder.
examples: I save money for emergencies — always have three months' worth. → estrategia concreta
She saves £200 a month automatically — direct debit. → método automatizado

questions.prompt: Rechazas una compra grande por motivos económicos.
questions.question: Complete: 'I can't ___ a new car right now.'
questions.explanation: 'Can't afford + sustantivo' = no puedo permitirme. Colocación fija clave. 'Expend' es formal/técnico (gastar recursos, no dinero personal). 'Cost' es 'costar' (sujeto es el producto). 'Price' es sustantivo. Estructura: 'afford + noun' o 'afford to + infinitive'.
examples: I can't afford a new phone this month — maybe next quarter. → aplazamiento
She can afford to travel first class — different tax bracket! → nivel adquisitivo

questions.statement: 'A budget' is a plan for how you spend your money.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Budget' = presupuesto, plan financiero personal o empresarial. Colocaciones: 'make/set a budget', 'stick to a budget', 'go over budget'. Falso amigo cuidado: en inglés NO significa 'barato' (eso es 'cheap' o 'low-cost'). 'Budget hotel' = hotel económico (colocación fija).
examples: I've made a budget for this month — no eating out. → decisión concreta
Sticking to a budget is important, especially with rent going up. → contexto actual

questions.text: Making a monthly budget helps you keep track of your expenses and save more.
questions.explanation: Nota 'making' con /ŋ/ nasal final. 'Monthly' /ˈmʌnθli/ con /θ/ sorda. 'Keep track of' se enlaza rápido con 'of' débil /əv/. Tres colocaciones financieras clave: 'make a budget', 'keep track of expenses', 'save more'. 'Keep track of' es fundamental para finanzas personales.
examples: I make a budget every month — Excel keeps me honest. → método concreto
Keep track of your spending — you'll be shocked what you spend on coffee. → observación

questions.prompt: Hablas de saldar completamente un préstamo estudiantil.
questions.question: Complete: 'I need to pay ___ my student loan.'
questions.explanation: 'Pay off + deuda' = saldar por completo. Phrasal verb fijo. Contraste: 'pay down' = reducir parcialmente. 'Pay up' es 'pagar lo que debes ya' (con presión). 'Pay away' no existe. Colocaciones: 'pay off a loan/mortgage/credit card/debt'. Meta financiera clásica.
examples: I want to pay off my credit card by the end of the year. → objetivo con plazo
She paid off her mortgage early — saved thousands in interest. → logro financiero

questions.prompt: Empareja cada término financiero con su definición:

pairs.right: use money to make more money

questions.explanation: Cuatro términos esenciales de finanzas personales B1. Distinción clave: 'save' es guardar sin riesgo; 'invest' es arriesgar para crecer. 'Budget' es planificar; 'debt' es deber dinero. Regla financiera básica: primero saldar debt, luego build savings, luego invest.
examples: I invest in index funds — low fees, long term. → estrategia moderna
He has a lot of debt from his university years. → contexto biográfico

questions.question: Choose: 'My monthly ___ is around 2000 euros.'
questions.explanation: 'Income' = ingresos (lo que ganas). 'Expenses' es lo que gastas — invertirían el sentido. 'Budget' es el plan. 'Debt' es deuda. Colocaciones: 'monthly/annual income', 'gross/net income', 'disposable income' (ingreso disponible tras gastos fijos).
examples: My monthly income has increased since the promotion. → mejora salarial
Her income is quite good but the cost of living is higher too. → matiz contextual

questions.target: I've been trying to save more money and reduce my monthly expenses.
questions.explanation: Situación: hablas de tus propósitos financieros en una charla casual o con tu asesor bancario. Present perfect continuous ('have been trying') destaca esfuerzo en curso. Dos colocaciones B1 clave: 'save more money' + 'reduce expenses'. Tono realista con 'trying' (no 'succeeding') — más creíble.
examples: I've been trying to save for a house deposit — slow going. → meta concreta con dificultad
She's been cutting down on expenses to pay off her card. → causa-efecto financiero

questions.statement: 'To be in debt' means to owe money to someone.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Be in debt' = deber dinero. Puede ser deuda con banco, tarjeta, préstamo estudiantil o persona. Colocaciones: 'get into debt', 'get out of debt', 'be up to your neck in debt' (endeudado hasta el cuello). 'Debt' /det/ con la 'b' muda — pronunciación traicionera.
examples: He's in debt because of his university studies. → origen de deuda
Many young people are in debt these days, unfortunately. → observación social

questions.prompt: Explicas cómo financiaste tu primera vivienda.
questions.question: Complete: 'I applied for a ___ to buy my first flat.'
questions.explanation: 'Loan' = préstamo (dinero prestado con compromiso de devolución + intereses). 'Debt' es la deuda resultante. 'Budget' es plan. 'Salary' es sueldo. Colocación fija: 'apply for a loan'. Tipos: personal loan, student loan, mortgage (préstamo hipotecario específico).
examples: I got a loan from the bank at 3.5% interest. → detalle financiero
She's still paying back her student loan five years later. → contexto temporal

questions.text: Investing your money wisely can help you build wealth over time.
questions.explanation: Nota 'wisely' /ˈwaɪzli/ con /aɪz/ diptongo. 'Build wealth' con /w/ enlazadas. 'Over time' con 'r' débil (UK). Tres colocaciones financieras avanzadas: 'invest wisely', 'build wealth', 'over time'. Discurso típico de asesores financieros. 'Wealth' es más formal que 'money' — implica riqueza acumulada.
examples: Invest wisely for the future — don't chase quick wins. → consejo prudente
Building wealth takes time and consistency — no shortcuts. → verdad financiera

questions.prompt: Identifica cuál es un hábito de gestión financiera.
questions.question: Which is a FINANCIAL HABIT?
questions.explanation: 'Setting a monthly budget' es hábito financiero clave — planificar antes de gastar. Las otras son actividades de ocio, no gestión de dinero. Colocación: 'set a budget' o 'make a budget'. Regla financiera básica: sin budget, no hay control real de gastos.
examples: Setting a budget helps you save consistently. → beneficio
A monthly budget improves your finances dramatically over a year. → impacto temporal

questions.statement: 'To live within your means' means to spend only what you can afford.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Live within your means' = no gastar más de lo que ganas — regla financiera clásica. 'Means' aquí = recursos económicos, no 'medios' de transporte. Idioma útil: 'live beyond your means' = vivir por encima de tus posibilidades (endeudarse). Discurso responsable, no juicio moral.
examples: It's important to live within your means, especially with rising costs. → contexto económico
She always lives within her means — no credit card debt ever. → hábito ejemplar

questions.question: Complete: 'You should have an emergency ___ for unexpected expenses.'
questions.explanation: 'Emergency fund' = fondo de emergencia — colocación fija financiera. Recomendación estándar: 3-6 meses de gastos. 'Debt/loan' invertirían el sentido (esas son problemas). 'Cost' no encaja. Colocaciones: 'build/set up/have an emergency fund'.
examples: Build an emergency fund for financial security — start small. → consejo práctico
An emergency fund saves you from stress when things go wrong. → beneficio emocional

questions.target: I'm saving up to buy a house within the next few years.
questions.explanation: Situación: alguien te pregunta por tus metas financieras. 'Save up for/to + meta' es phrasal verb clave — 'up' intensifica la acumulación. 'Within the next few years' proyecta plazo realista. Contracción 'I'm' natural en habla. Tono seguro pero flexible, sin dar cifras exactas.
examples: I'm saving up for a new car — hopefully by summer. → meta con plazo
We're saving up to travel around Asia next year — the dream trip. → meta compartida
